a: The most isolated inhabited place on Earth is generally considered to be Tristan da Cunha, a volcanic island in the South Atlantic Ocean. Located roughly 2,400 kilometers (1,500 miles) west of Cape Town, South Africa, and 3,360 kilometers (2,090 miles) east of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, it is the most remote island in the world with a permanent population. The island has about 250 year-round residents who live in the settlement of Edinburgh of the Seven Seas. Supplies arrive only every six weeks by ship from Cape Town, and the nearest other inhabited land is over 2,000 kilometers away. In addition, extremely isolated inhabited places include Easter Island, Pitcairn Island, and Campbell Island, but Tristan da Cunha holds the record for the greatest distance from any other human settlement.

a: The most isolated inhabited places on Earth include Tristan da Cunha in the South Atlantic, which is the most remote island with a permanent population of about 250 people. Easter Island in the Pacific, famous for its moai statues, is another extremely isolated location with around 70,000 residents. The Pitcairn Islands, settled by descendants of the Bounty mutineers, have a population of about 50 people and are among the most remote inhabited places. Campbell Island, south of New Zealand, was inhabited until 1992 and is now uninhabited but was once one of the most isolated settlements. These locations are characterized by their vast distance from major landmasses, limited supply routes, and small, self-sufficient communities.
